chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Kazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Jabir ibn Abdullah: 'O Jabir! This is the month of Ramadan. Whoever fasts its day, stands in prayer from its night, keeps his belly and private parts chaste, and restrains his tongue, will emerge from his sins as he emerged from the month.' So Jabir said: 'O Messenger of Allah! How beautiful is this hadith!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Jabir! And how severe/difficult are these conditions.'

key_terms.عَفَّ بَطْنُهُ وَ فَرْجُهُ: Kept his belly and private parts chaste

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for complete forgiveness of sins during Ramadan according to the Prophet (SAWW)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes that Ramadan fasting is not merely abstention from food but a holistic discipline involving the guarding of the stomach, private parts, and tongue, leading to a complete cleansing of sins. The Prophet’s follow-up remark underscores the rigorous nature of these conditions, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that true spiritual purification requires active, conscious effort across all faculties. This narrative serves as a practical guide for believers to elevate their worship beyond ritualistic form to comprehensive moral and spiritual excellence.
